transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-08-20
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Quantaco ML Eng), Liam O'Neill (Quantaco Infra), Rahul Sen (Quantaco CTO)

Summary (auto): quick check on cost/unit economics; go over benchmark numbers, clarify metrics (tokens/sec/$), decide next benchmark runs and artifacts to share.

00:00 - Sasha Patel: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, short agenda today is cost run through, caching results, and pick next experiment
00:12 - Maya Chen: yeah thanks, been looking forward to the numbers, we're trying to understand whether we tune batching or invest in dedicated nodes
00:28 - Diego Ramos: cool, i'll go through the numbers i ran last night, quick caveat transcription might garble some terms like kv-cache or kernal names
00:38 - Diego Ramos: baseline - hosted model rtx-like instance, no caching, batch size 1: about 220 tokens/sec sustained, roughly $0.80 per 1k tokens based on our internal hosted rates -> converting that's about 275 tokens / $ / sec (i say that loosely as tokens per second per dollar metric)
01:05 - Liam O'Neill: sorry can you repeat the tokens / $ / sec calculation? i'm trying to map to our cost target
01:12 - Diego Ramos: yeah so if you're getting 220 tokens/sec and paying say $0.80 per 1k tokens, that's 220 * 1000 / 0.80 = 275k tokens/sec per dollar? (note: rough math in call) i may have misspoken, the easier way is tokens per dollar per hour etc. the sheet i'll send normalizes to tokens/sec/$ properly
01:40 - Rahul Sen: main question is with caching/prefix reuse our effective tokens emitted to the model drop a lot, so billing goes down. show us caching numbers
01:50 - Diego Ramos: right, so with KV/prefix caching enabled and a moderate prefix hit rate (~35% of tokens from cache) we measured 420 tokens/sec user-visible throughput, and cost per emitted token dropped ~28% vs baseline. that came from less decoder work and better batching
02:20 - Sasha Patel: to be clear, the 420 tokens/sec is observed at batch size 8 with caching enabled on the same infra
02:30 - Maya Chen: latency impact? we're constrained to ~250ms 95th p99 for our agent flows
02:36 - Diego Ramos: p95 was 230ms at batch 8 with caching, p99 ~380ms; so p99 is above your 250ms SLO but p95 is under. with batch 1 and caching p99 dropped to ~270ms but throughput dropped to ~260 tokens/sec
03:05 - Liam O'Neill: so batching helps throughput/cost but hurts p99; what's the tokens/sec/$ delta at batch8 vs batch1
03:12 - Diego Ramos: batch1 no cache: 220 t/s, batch8 no cache: 520 t/s; batch1 with cache: 260 t/s, batch8 with cache: 420 t/s. cost per 1M tokens baseline $800 (hosted), with batch8+cache effective cost per 1M tokens ~ $580 -> roughly 27.5% savings
03:45 - Maya Chen: good, that moves us toward the budget, but we need tighter p99
03:50 - Diego Ramos: options: 1) use smaller batch size for tail-sensitive routes (route-based batching), 2) intelligent routing to Dedicated for high-SLA traffic, 3) rework prompts to increase prefix reuse
04:10 - Sasha Patel: also quantization/seq-length tuning helps; we saw additional 10% gains using int8 path for this model, Diego?
04:18 - Diego Ramos: yep int8 quant gave ~1.1x throughput improvement and about 8-12% cost reduction depending on model fidelity tradeoffs
04:30 - Rahul Sen: if we considered Dedicated, what does the TCO look like for our pilot 50M tokens/mo?
04:40 - Sasha Patel: rough numbers - hosted at current rates and observed caching would be around $40K/month for 50M tokens at baseline, with caching+batching we estimate $29K/mo. Dedicated reserved for similar throughput with 3-month commit could drop to ~$14-18K/mo depending on GPU class and utilization
05:05 - Liam O'Neill: that's a big swing, but dedicated has infra ops overhead and commit risk
05:12 - Sasha Patel: yes, which is why we propose to run a Dedicated estimate only if the SE benchmark shows >2x improvement in tokens/sec/$ over hosted with caching
05:22 - Diego Ramos: for the benchmark plan i propose: 1-hour runs x 3 batch sizes (1,8,32) with caching on/off, capture token throughput, p95/p99 latency, and cost counters. i'll instrument with KV hit rates and prefix reuse histograms
05:40 - Maya Chen: can you also log payload sizes and prompt length distribution? those matter a lot
05:46 - Diego Ramos: yes will capture prompt length hist & tail percentiles
05:52 - Rahul Sen: what about model variants / smaller model family? tradeoffs?
05:56 - Diego Ramos: we tried a distilled variant as well — throughput improved ~1.8x but generation quality dropped on longer reasoning prompts; we can provide evals vs your prompt set
06:10 - Maya Chen: we care about hallucination for some flows, so quality hit is a blocker unless we can test vs QC prompts
06:18 - Sasha Patel: agreed. next steps: bench w/ sample prompts, AE sends pricing worksheet, customer shares prompts
06:24 - Liam O'Neill: one more thing — are audit logs and SSO included for Dedicated pilot? need to confirm with security
06:30 - Sasha Patel: yes Dedicated pilot includes basic audit logs and SAML SSO; for advanced retention or HSM we can add enterprise package
06:38 - Maya Chen: timeline: if we get the bench results by Fri (2025-08-22) we can decide on Dedicated PO next week
06:44 - Diego Ramos: i'll schedule the runs tonight and share logs in the drive; expecting to upload around EOD 2025-08-21
06:52 - Sasha Patel: perfect. recap of action items and i'll drop the pricing sheet in CRM

07:10 - Sasha Patel: thanks all, we'll sync Wed next week if needed
